title: Role Segmentation Matrix and Telemetry Spec
summary: Practical guidance and a compact role matrix for segmenting IAM privileges across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments plus a minimal, SIEM-friendly audit schema and an evidence automation checklist.
body:
Purpose:
This doc provides: a) a concise role segmentation matrix mapped to common Redwood personas and environment types (hosted / dedicated / private), b) small, copy-paste policy templates for common delegation scenarios, c) a normalized audit event schema designed for SIEM export and evidence automation, and d) an operational checklist for evidence collection and automated proof generation. Goal is to reduce ad-hoc access requests and produce machine-friendly telemetry for compliance reviews.

Assumptions and definitions:
- Persona = human or service role type (e.g., ML-Engineer, Platform-Oncall, SRE, Customer-Admin).
- Environment types: Hosted (shared Redwood multi-tenant control plane), Dedicated (customer-reserved capacity under Redwood management), Private (customer-managed VPC/on-prem with customer control plane).
- Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP) and Separation of Duties (SoD) are applied by default.

1) Role Segmentation Matrix (compact view)
Columns: Persona | Read | Operate | Deploy | Audit | Admin-Level
- ML-Engineer | Model-read, Logs-read | Inference-invoke, Job-submit | Model-version-push (canary only) | Evidence-read | none
- Platform-Oncall | Metrics-read, Traces-read | Route-traffic, Fallback-config | none | Evidence-read, Evidence-export | none
- SRE | Infra-read, Logs-read | Restart-nodes, Scale-pools | none | Evidence-read, Audit-trigger | none
- Solutions-Engineer (Customer-facing) | Customer-config-read | Customer-config-edit (scoped) | none | Evidence-read (customer-scoped) | none
- Customer-Admin (Dedicated/Private) | Customer-config-read | Customer-config-edit, Capacity-change | Model-version-push (customer-owned) | Evidence-request | Owner-role (for private)
- Security-Admin | Org-config-read | Policy-enforce | none | Evidence-read, Retention-config | Org-admin (sensitive)
Notes:
- "Model-version-push" for Hosted is restricted to an allowlist of verified builders; in Dedicated/Private the customer may own this.
- Admin-Level entries indicate where SoD breaks are permitted and require approval workflow.

2) Environment-specific delegation patterns (high-level guidance)
Hosted:
- No direct host-level SSH or hypervisor access. All operational actions happen through audited control plane APIs.
- Customer-facing roles map to RBAC scopes that include a tenant_id claim. Policies must include "tenant_id" condition to prevent cross-tenant operations.
Dedicated:
- Two-tier admin model: Redwood infra-admin (platform) vs customer-admin (tenant). Policies must encode scope: resource.project_id == customer_project or resource.pool_id == dedicated_pool.
Private:
- Default posture: customer owner administers the control plane. Redwood support roles may be given temporary delegated roles via time-bound tokens and recorded evidence workflows (see evidence automation).

3) Policy template snippets (JSON-esque ACL examples; replace placeholders)
- Tenant-scoped read-only policy (Hosted):
  Effect: Allow
  Actions: ["controlplane.models:read", "controlplane.logs:search"]
  Resource: ["arn:redwood:tenant:${tenant_id}:*"]
  Condition: {"StringEquals": {"request.origin": "control-plane"}}

- Dedicated pool admin (scoped):
  Effect: Allow
  Actions: ["dedicated.pool:scale", "dedicated.pool:drain"]
  Resource: ["arn:redwood:dedicated:${pool_id}"]
  Condition: {"Bool": {"request.approval_granted": "true"}}

- Temporary support escalation (Private):
  Effect: Allow
  Actions: ["private.node:connect", "private.trace:collect"]
  Resource: ["arn:redwood:private:${customer_id}:*"]
  Condition: {"DateLessThan": {"request.expire_at": "${expiry_ts}"}, "StringEquals": {"request.ticket": "${jira_id}"}}

4) Audit / SIEM-ready event schema (minimal normalized fields)
Design goal: compact fields, fixed names, indexes for fast queries. Map source logs to these fields before shipping to SIEM.
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC string
- event_id: global unique id (uuid)
- actor_id: principal identifier (user:<email> | svc:<name>)
- actor_type: user | service | support-bot
- action: canonical action name (e.g., models.read, pools.scale, login.sso)
- resource_type: model | pool | tenant | node | secret
- resource_id: canonical resource ARN or id
- environment: hosted | dedicated | private
- outcome: success | failure | partial
- ip: ip address or cidr (if available)
- request_id: upstream request correlation id (if present)
- policy_evaluated: allow | deny | conditional
- policy_ids: list of policy identifiers that matched (comma-separated string)
- justification_ticket: jira ticket id or support ticket id (optional)
- retention_label: e.g., pii | low | high (used to route to evidence storage)
- raw_payload: truncated JSON blob (max 16KB) for forensics

Example event line (JSON):
{
  "timestamp": "2025-01-22T18:44:12Z",
  "event_id": "b7c2f3a2-3d4b-11ec-9d74-0242ac120002",
  "actor_id": "user:marco.chen@redwood.com",
  "actor_type": "user",
  "action": "pools.scale",
  "resource_type": "dedicated_pool",
  "resource_id": "arn:redwood:dedicated:pool:eu-west-1:pool-42",
  "environment": "dedicated",
  "outcome": "success",
  "ip": "34.22.11.7",
  "request_id": "req-0a1b2c3d",
  "policy_evaluated": "allow",
  "policy_ids": "pol-234,pol-800",
  "justification_ticket": "JIRA-SEC-3347",
  "retention_label": "low",
  "raw_payload": "{"cpu_request": 12, "scale_from": 4, "scale_to": 12}"
}

5) SIEM export mapping recommendations
- Export normalized events into the SIEM index named: redwood-events-{environment} with daily rollover.
- Use event_id as the primary deduplication key.
- Create pre-built parsers for each environment that map vendor fields to the normalized schema.
- Create saved searches/alerts for: multiple failed policy_evaluated==deny per actor_id in 10m; escalation events (temporary support tokens created); cross-tenant operations attempts in Hosted environment.

6) Evidence automation runbook (for audit requests and periodic reviews)
Goal: produce tamper-evident packages for reviewers with minimal manual steps.
Steps:
- Trigger: periodic (30d) or on-demand via Jira ticket JIRA-SEC-AUDIT-xxx.
- Query SIEM for events matching tenant_id or resource set + time window.
- Pull linked artifacts: control-plane request logs, job payloads, model-version manifests, approval ticket metadata.
- Package: store events + artifacts into WORM storage bucket with write-once metadata including collector_id and hash of the package.
- Sign: attach HSM-signed hash and create audit record with package_id.
- Deliver: egress package to reviewer group with ACLs and time-limited signed URL.
- Retention: follow retention_label. Automatic retention purge must be gated by a retention-review job and recorded as an event.

Automation pointers:
- Use the policy_ids field to filter for policy-coverage checks.
- For Hosted tenant evidence, always include tenant-scoped resource filters to avoid leaking other tenants.
- When creating temporary support tokens, require a ticket id and record it in the event.justification_ticket field.

7) Quick verification checklist (pre-audit)
- [ ] All role definitions are in IAM repo and referenced by policy_id.
- [ ] SIEM normalization pipeline maps the list of fields in section 4.
- [ ] Evidence automation pipeline can produce a signed package within 30 minutes for a single tenant time window.
- [ ] Time-bound tokens are rejected after expiry and generate an audit event with outcome=failure.
- [ ] Cross-tenant attempts in Hosted environment generate alerts and an automated incident ticket.

8) Open decisions / TODOs
- Decide canonical naming for policy_ids (short id vs full path). Recommendation: short prefix pol-<number> for storage efficiency.
- Retention labels mapping to legal/regulatory policies per region (E.U. vs US) needs consolidation with Legal.
- Evaluate whether raw_payload should be stored inline or referenced via object store to meet privacy budgets.

Appendix: Helpful copy-paste snippets and references
- Recommended SIEM index lifecycle: hot (7d), warm (23d), cold (365d), frozen (archive).
- Example alert: "hosted.cross_tenant_access_attempt" triggers when resource.environment==hosted AND policy_evaluated==allow AND resource.tenant_id != actor.tenant_id.
- Minimal fields for evidence package manifest: package_id, tenant_id, time_window, collected_by, sha256_sum, signed_by.

Contact: security-and-compliance channel or Aisha Rao (aisha@redwood.com) for questions or to request changes.
